Replay

Tagged value unions

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Canonical representationPublic projections and variant changesReplay and diagnosticsAcceptance

Use ordinary Odin tagged unions or union #no_nil when actions, controls, events or state need typed alternatives. Replay supports them when every possible variant is a supported owned value:

Odin
Take :: struct {amount: u32}
Put :: struct {amount: u32}
Action :: union {Take, Put}

apply :: proc(action: Action) {
    switch value in action {
    case Take: // value.amount belongs to Take
    case Put:  // value.amount belongs to Put
    case:      // nil: no action
    }
}

There is no second handwritten enum or a set of unrelated argument fields to keep in sync. Reference-bearing variants, raw unions, shared-nil unions, unsupported scalar types and platform-width wire integers remain rejected. Validation examines all possible variants, including hidden fields and zero-length arrays. Merely leaving a forbidden variant inactive does not make its type safe.

Canonical representation#

Each union occupies a fixed-width canonical region:

  • A four-byte little-endian tag: 0 means nil, and 1..N follow declaration order.
  • A payload area as large as the largest projected variant.
  • The active variant's canonical fields at the start of that area.
  • Zero bytes in the remaining payload area. A nil value has an all-zero payload.

The fixed representation fits the existing bounded frame/snapshot/delta programs. It does not transmit native union padding, inactive values or native tag width. For #no_nil, zero is invalid on the wire; the native zero-based discriminator is mapped to the same one-based canonical tags. Variant names, declaration order, nullability and field layouts participate in the schema fingerprint. Named variants include their package/name; compiler pointers and source locations never enter it.

Schema construction builds conditional field metadata. Encoding validates only the active value, then writes a zeroed canonical region. Decoding checks all active tags/scalars and every unused tail byte before changing its destination. A malformed tag, active enum/bool/float or nonzero unused tail fails transactionally. Nested unions are conditional on their entire enclosing variant chain.

Schemas without unions retain their existing fingerprints, bytes and contiguous copy program. No global protocol version changes solely to add this type support. A game changing its declared types still needs its own schema/content compatibility transition; existing peers cannot silently reinterpret a new union shape.

Public projections and variant changes#

An authority-only union field is entirely excluded from a public projection. Private fields inside a public union variant are omitted from the payload, while the variant choice remains visible. Annotate the whole union if its choice is also private information.

Public decode preserves private local fields when the active variant stays the same. On a variant change, it zero-initializes the union's native storage before installing the new tag and public fields. It does not reinterpret old private bytes as a different variant. Private fields in a newly selected variant therefore need appropriate application defaults/validation if zero is not meaningful for them. This is explicit initialization, not reconstruction of hidden authority state.

Nilable unions are a useful default for actions/events and unused fixed storage. For #no_nil, the zero-initialized first variant must be valid wherever the program uses zero-filled values; an enum without a zero member still needs initialization.

Replay and diagnostics#

Local frame storage recursively admits only value-safe variants. State/input/event copies and replay restore the selected variant with the rest of the world. Odin's logical comparison ignores inactive variant storage; canonical encoding also ignores that storage and makes its wire tail deterministic.

Field diffs expose a $tag entry plus conditional variant paths. A switch can report a field becoming inactive even if both its numeric bit values happen to be zero. Difference.left_present/right_present distinguish absence from a real zero; diff_value prints <inactive> for that side. Consumers should retain the schema while using its borrowed diagnostic metadata.

Acceptance#

tests/replay_unions/run.sh executes a union-valued state/input/event corpus, revises an earlier input and checks identical schema fingerprints, canonical bytes and final hashes in native default/optimized builds and actual WASM execution. On the tested ARM64 Mac, an x86-64 binary executed through Rosetta agrees too.

tests/replay_unions/enet_run.sh runs separate Godot host/client processes with union-valued state, controls, actions and events under latency, jitter, loss and duplication. Both see four accepted transfers, conserve inventory and compare the same final world. The in-memory network suite additionally covers checkpoint capture/decode/restore and local audit of that model.

These tests establish the stated type/codec/runner behavior on the recorded targets. They do not establish every OS, every user union layout, an unbounded dynamic-state model or full roadmap completion. See the recorded union evidence.
